name: Smooth local representations and GL₂ automorphic representations
purpose: A family of proposed roadmaps that overlap one another or existing Tau Ceti roadmaps. Restructure it so that every piece of mathematics has exactly one owner and the roadmaps build on each other (research/blueprint/PROTOCOL.md section 15).
method: Members are the proposed roadmaps joined by strong overlaps (at least half of one roadmap's layers, and at least three layers); anchors are the Tau Ceti roadmaps a member overlaps in at least three layers (or two and 40% of its layers). Evidence: duplicate records of the reviewed and unreviewed library audits, and 'rescope' overlaps of the link maps. Leads, not verdicts.

anchors.title: Modular forms — Hecke theory, newforms, and L-functions

Proves the local GL2 conductor/newvector theorem with the principal-series/special/supercuspidal classification and twist calculations: the local form of this layer's conductor and bad-prime eigenvalue classification.
Strong multiplicity one and multiplicity one for newforms, whose fixed-level form Tau Ceti has already proved: the classical GL₂/ℚ version of R16.4's multiplicity statements.
Proves that coefficient fields of newforms are number fields via modular symbols and the integral Hecke algebra, R16.4's rationality target over ℚ.

Hecke's completed L-function and functional equation for newforms of level N with the Atkin–Lehner sign, the existing classical L-function R16.5 compares with. Its continuation is already in Mathlib and Tau Ceti.
The classical newforms, primitive forms and conductor that R16.6 identifies with automorphic representations. Most of this layer is built in Tau Ceti.
The Eichler–Selberg trace formula for Hecke operators, the classical GL₂ trace identity, planned by an elementary route. It overlaps R17.2's GL₂ specialization of the trace formula.
